30! **************************************************************************
31512512 subroutine rrtmg_sw_ini
32! **************************************************************************
33!
34! Original version: Michael J. Iacono; February, 2004
35! Revision for F90 formatting: M. J. Iacono, July, 2006
36!
37! This subroutine performs calculations necessary for the initialization
38! of the shortwave model. Lookup tables are computed for use in the SW
39! radiative transfer, and input absorption coefficient data for each
40! spectral band are reduced from 224 g-point intervals to 112.
41! **************************************************************************
42
43 use parrrsw, only : mg, nbndsw, ngptsw
44 use rrsw_tbl, only: ntbl, tblint, pade, bpade, tau_tbl, exp_tbl
45 use rrsw_vsn, only: hvrini, hnamini
46
47! ------- Local -------
48
49 integer :: ibnd, igc, ig, ind, ipr
50 integer :: igcsm, iprsm
51 integer :: itr
52
53 real(kind=r8) :: wtsum, wtsm(mg)
54 real(kind=r8) :: tfn
55
56! ------- Definitions -------
57! Arrays for 10000-point look-up tables:
58! TAU_TBL Clear-sky optical depth
59! EXP_TBL Exponential lookup table for transmittance
60! PADE Pade approximation constant (= 0.278)
61! BPADE Inverse of the Pade approximation constant
62!
63
64512512 hvrini = '$Revision: 1.2 $'
65
66! Initialize model data
67512512 call swdatinit
68512512 call swcmbdat ! g-point interval reduction data
69512512 call swaerpr ! aerosol optical properties
70512512 call swcldpr ! cloud optical properties
71512512 call swatmref ! reference MLS profile
72512512 call sw_kgb16 ! molecular absorption coefficients
73512512 call sw_kgb17
74512512 call sw_kgb18
75512512 call sw_kgb19
76512512 call sw_kgb20
77512512 call sw_kgb21
78512512 call sw_kgb22
79512512 call sw_kgb23
80512512 call sw_kgb24
81512512 call sw_kgb25
82512512 call sw_kgb26
83512512 call sw_kgb27
84512512 call sw_kgb28
85512512 call sw_kgb29
86
87! Define exponential lookup tables for transmittance. Tau is
88! computed as a function of the tau transition function, and transmittance
89! is calculated as a function of tau. All tables are computed at intervals
90! of 0.0001. The inverse of the constant used in the Pade approximation to
91! the tau transition function is set to bpade.
92
93512512 exp_tbl(0) = 1.0_r8
94 exp_tbl(ntbl) = 0.0_r8
95 bpade = 1.0_r8 / pade
9651194885119488 do itr = 1, ntbl-1
9751194885119488 tfn = float(itr) / float(ntbl)
98 tau_tbl = bpade * tfn / (1._r8 - tfn)
99 exp_tbl(itr) = exp(-tau_tbl)
100 enddo
101
102! Perform g-point reduction from 16 per band (224 total points) to
103! a band dependent number (112 total points) for all absorption
104! coefficient input data and Planck fraction input data.
105! Compute relative weighting for new g-point combinations.
106
107512512 igcsm = 0
10871687168 do ibnd = 1,nbndsw
10971687168 iprsm = 0
110 if (ngc(ibnd).lt.mg) then
1115734464512 do igc = 1,ngc(ibnd)
1125734457344 igcsm = igcsm + 1
113 wtsum = 0.
114114688114688 do ipr = 1, ngn(igcsm)
115 iprsm = iprsm + 1
116 wtsum = wtsum + wt(iprsm)
117 enddo
118 wtsm(igc) = wtsum
119 enddo
120114688121856 do ig = 1, ng(ibnd+15)
121 ind = (ibnd-1)*mg + ig
122 rwgt(ind) = wt(ig)/wtsm(ngm(ind))
123 enddo
124 else
12500 do ig = 1, ng(ibnd+15)
126 igcsm = igcsm + 1
127 ind = (ibnd-1)*mg + ig
128 rwgt(ind) = 1.0_r8
129 enddo
130 endif
131 enddo
132
133! Reduce g-points for absorption coefficient data in each LW spectral band.
134
135512512 call cmbgb16s
136512512 call cmbgb17
137512512 call cmbgb18
138512512 call cmbgb19
139512512 call cmbgb20
140512512 call cmbgb21
141512512 call cmbgb22
142512512 call cmbgb23
143512512 call cmbgb24
144512512 call cmbgb25
145512512 call cmbgb26
146512512 call cmbgb27
147512512 call cmbgb28
148512512 call cmbgb29
149
150512512 end subroutine rrtmg_sw_ini

152!***************************************************************************
153512512 subroutine swdatinit
154!***************************************************************************
155
156! --------- Modules ----------
157
158 use rrsw_con, only: heatfac, grav, planck, boltz, &
159 clight, avogad, alosmt, gascon, radcn1, radcn2
160 use rrsw_wvn, only: ng, nspa, nspb, wavenum1, wavenum2, delwave
161 use shr_const_mod, only: shr_const_avogad
162 use physconst, only: cday, gravit, cpair
163 use rrsw_vsn
164
165 save
166
167! Shortwave spectral band limits (wavenumbers)
16871688192 wavenum1(:) = (/2600._r8, 3250._r8, 4000._r8, 4650._r8, 5150._r8, 6150._r8, 7700._r8, &
169 8050._r8,12850._r8,16000._r8,22650._r8,29000._r8,38000._r8, 820._r8/)
17071688192 wavenum2(:) = (/3250._r8, 4000._r8, 4650._r8, 5150._r8, 6150._r8, 7700._r8, 8050._r8, &
171 12850._r8,16000._r8,22650._r8,29000._r8,38000._r8,50000._r8, 2600._r8/)
17271688192 delwave(:) = (/ 650._r8, 750._r8, 650._r8, 500._r8, 1000._r8, 1550._r8, 350._r8, &
173 4800._r8, 3150._r8, 6650._r8, 6350._r8, 9000._r8,12000._r8, 1780._r8/)
174
175! Spectral band information
17671688192 ng(:) = (/16,16,16,16,16,16,16,16,16,16,16,16,16,16/)
17771688192 nspa(:) = (/9,9,9,9,1,9,9,1,9,1,0,1,9,1/)
17871688192 nspb(:) = (/1,5,1,1,1,5,1,0,1,0,0,1,5,1/)
179
180! Use constants set in CAM for consistency
181512512 grav = gravit
182 avogad = shr_const_avogad * 1.e-3_r8
183
184! Heatfac is the factor by which one must multiply delta-flux/
185! delta-pressure, with flux in w/m-2 and pressure in mbar, to get
186! the heating rate in units of degrees/day. It is equal to
187! (g)x(#sec/day)x(1e-5)/(specific heat of air at const. p)
188! = (9.8066)(86400)(1e-5)/(1.004)
189! heatfac = 8.4391_r8
190
191! Modified values for consistency with CAM3:
192! = (9.80616)(86400)(1e-5)/(1.00464)
193! heatfac = 8.43339130434_r8
194
195! Calculate heatfac directly from CAM constants:
196 heatfac = grav * cday * 1.e-5_r8 / (cpair * 1.e-3_r8)
197
198! Constants from NIST 01/11/2002
199
200! grav = 9.8066_r8
201 planck = 6.62606876e-27_r8
202 boltz = 1.3806503e-16_r8
203 clight = 2.99792458e+10_r8
204! avogad = 6.02214199e+23_r8
205 alosmt = 2.6867775e+19_r8
206 gascon = 8.31447200e+07_r8
207 radcn1 = 1.191042722e-12_r8
208 radcn2 = 1.4387752_r8
209
210!
211! units are generally cgs
212!
213! The first and second radiation constants are taken from NIST.
214! They were previously obtained from the relations:
215! radcn1 = 2.*planck*clight*clight*1.e-07
216! radcn2 = planck*clight/boltz
217
218512512 end subroutine swdatinit

228! ------- Definitions -------
229! Arrays for the g-point reduction from 224 to 112 for the 16 LW bands:
230! This mapping from 224 to 112 points has been carefully selected to
231! minimize the effect on the resulting fluxes and cooling rates, and
232! caution should be used if the mapping is modified. The full 224
233! g-point set can be restored with ngpt=224, ngc=16*16, ngn=224*1., etc.
234! ngpt The total number of new g-points

236! ngs The cumulative sum of new g-points for each band

348!***************************************************************************
349512512 subroutine cmbgb16s
350!***************************************************************************
351!
352! Original version: MJIacono; July 1998
353! Revision for RRTM_SW: MJIacono; November 2002
354! Revision for RRTMG_SW: MJIacono; December 2003
355! Revision for F90 reformatting: MJIacono; July 2006
356!
357! The subroutines CMBGB16->CMBGB29 input the absorption coefficient
358! data for each band, which are defined for 16 g-points and 14 spectral
359! bands. The data are combined with appropriate weighting following the
360! g-point mapping arrays specified in RRTMG_SW_INIT. Solar source
361! function data in array SFLUXREF are combined without weighting. All
362! g-point reduced data are put into new arrays for use in RRTMG_SW.
363!
364! band 16: 2600-3250 cm-1 (low key- h2o,ch4; high key - ch4)
365!
366!-----------------------------------------------------------------------
367
368 use rrsw_wvn, only : ngc, ngs, ngn, wt, rwgt
369 use rrsw_kg16, only : kao, kbo, selfrefo, forrefo, sfluxrefo, &
370 ka, kb, selfref, forref, sfluxref
371
372! ------- Local -------
373 integer :: jn, jt, jp, igc, ipr, iprsm
374 real(kind=r8) :: sumk, sumf
375
376
37746085120 do jn = 1,9
3782304027648 do jt = 1,5
379299520322560 do jp = 1,13
380299520299520 iprsm = 0
38117971201797120 do igc = 1,ngc(1)
38217971201797120 sumk = 0.
38347923204792320 do ipr = 1, ngn(igc)
384 iprsm = iprsm + 1
385 sumk = sumk + kao(jn,jt,jp,iprsm)*rwgt(iprsm)
386 enddo
387 ka(jn,jt,jp,igc) = sumk
388 enddo
389 enddo
390 enddo
391 enddo
392
39325603072 do jt = 1,5
394120320122880 do jp = 13,59
395120320120320 iprsm = 0
396721920721920 do igc = 1,ngc(1)
397721920721920 sumk = 0.
39819251201925120 do ipr = 1, ngn(igc)
399 iprsm = iprsm + 1
400 sumk = sumk + kbo(jt,jp,iprsm)*rwgt(iprsm)
401 enddo
402 kb(jt,jp,igc) = sumk
403 enddo
404 enddo
405 enddo
406
40751205632 do jt = 1,10
40851205120 iprsm = 0
4093072030720 do igc = 1,ngc(1)
4103072030720 sumk = 0.
4118192081920 do ipr = 1, ngn(igc)
412 iprsm = iprsm + 1
413 sumk = sumk + selfrefo(jt,iprsm)*rwgt(iprsm)
414 enddo
415 selfref(jt,igc) = sumk
416 enddo
417 enddo
418
41915362048 do jt = 1,3
42015361536 iprsm = 0
42192169216 do igc = 1,ngc(1)
42292169216 sumk = 0.
4232457624576 do ipr = 1, ngn(igc)
424 iprsm = iprsm + 1
425 sumk = sumk + forrefo(jt,iprsm)*rwgt(iprsm)
426 enddo
427 forref(jt,igc) = sumk
428 enddo
429 enddo
430
431512512 iprsm = 0
43230723072 do igc = 1,ngc(1)
43330723072 sumf = 0.
43481928192 do ipr = 1, ngn(igc)
435 iprsm = iprsm + 1
436 sumf = sumf + sfluxrefo(iprsm)
437 enddo
438 sfluxref(igc) = sumf
439 enddo
440
441512512 end subroutine cmbgb16s

443!***************************************************************************
444512512 subroutine cmbgb17
445!***************************************************************************
446!
447! band 17: 3250-4000 cm-1 (low - h2o,co2; high - h2o,co2)
448!-----------------------------------------------------------------------
449

1511!***********************************************************************
1512512512 subroutine swcldpr
1513!***********************************************************************
1514
1515! Purpose: Define cloud extinction coefficient, single scattering albedo
1516! and asymmetry parameter data.
1517!
1518
1519! ------- Modules -------
1520
1521 use rrsw_cld, only : extliq1, ssaliq1, asyliq1, &
1522 extice2, ssaice2, asyice2, &
1523 extice3, ssaice3, asyice3, fdlice3, &
1524 abari, bbari, cbari, dbari, ebari, fbari
1525
1526 save
1527
1528!-----------------------------------------------------------------------
1529!
1530! Explanation of the method for each value of INFLAG. A value of
1531! 0 for INFLAG do not distingish being liquid and ice clouds.
1532! INFLAG = 2 does distinguish between liquid and ice clouds, and
1533! requires further user input to specify the method to be used to
1534! compute the aborption due to each.
1535! INFLAG = 0: For each cloudy layer, the cloud fraction, the cloud optical
1536! depth, the cloud single-scattering albedo, and the
1537! moments of the phase function (0:NSTREAM). Note
1538! that these values are delta-m scaled within this
1539! subroutine.
1540
1541! INFLAG = 2: For each cloudy layer, the cloud fraction, cloud
1542! water path (g/m2), and cloud ice fraction are input.
1543! ICEFLAG = 2: The ice effective radius (microns) is input and the
1544! optical properties due to ice clouds are computed from
1545! the optical properties stored in the RT code, STREAMER v3.0
1546! (Reference: Key. J., Streamer User's Guide, Cooperative
1547! Institute for Meteorological Satellite Studies, 2001, 96 pp.).
1548! Valid range of values for re are between 5.0 and
1549! 131.0 micron.
